states.say: Presentation 0 of the force density method of Klaus Linkwitz and Hans-Jörg Schek: before any matrix, the equilibrium of one node.
states.title: Equilibrium of a node

states.say: Two cables run from supports $A$ and $B$ to a node $n$. A load of $p = 10$ kN hangs there.
states.title: A load on two cables

states.say: A cable can only pull, and only along itself. How hard does each cable pull?
states.title: A load on two cables

states.say: The node does not move, so the three forces cancel.
states.title: A load on two cables

states.say: Equilibrium.
states.title: A load on two cables

states.say: Draw the load to scale: 10 kN is 4 units.
states.title: By drawing · the force diagram

states.say: From its tip, draw $f_2$ parallel to cable 2.
states.title: By drawing · the force diagram

states.say: Then $f_1$, parallel to cable 1, back to the start. The polygon is **closed**.
states.title: By drawing · the force diagram

states.say: Measure the sides and divide by the scale.
states.title: By drawing · the force diagram

states.say: Now without a ruler. On the left is the geometry: cable 1 runs 4 across and 3 up, so its length is 5.
states.title: By computing · the projections

states.say: Its angles to the $x$ and $y$ directions. A cosine is the side along that direction over the length.
states.title: By computing · the projections

states.say: On the right is the force diagram. $f_1$ is parallel to cable 1, so the same angles split it. Its $x$ part points left: minus.
states.title: By computing · the projections

states.say: Cable 2 the same way: 3 across, 4 up, length 5.
states.title: By computing · the projections

states.say: In the force diagram, both parts of $f_2$ point the positive way: right and up.
states.title: By computing · the projections

states.say: Along $x$ the two parts are equal and opposite: they cancel.
states.title: By computing · equilibrium

states.say: Along $y$ the two parts stack up to the height of the load.
states.title: By computing · equilibrium

states.say: Two equations, two unknowns. The first gives $f_1 = 0.75 f_2$. Put that into the second.
states.title: By computing · equilibrium

states.say: Check along $x$: $-4.8 + 4.8 = 0$. Along $y$: $3.6 + 6.4 - 10 = 0$. The drawing gave the same 6 kN and 8 kN.
states.title: By computing · equilibrium

states.say: A closed force polygon and zero sums of projections say the same thing. In space there is a third sum, along $z$: the next presentation.
states.title: By computing · equilibrium
